title: Development and characterization of l‐cysteine incorporated gelatin–carboxymethylcellulose hydrogel for extending the shelf life of button mushrooms
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

This study investigated gelatin–carboxymethyl cellulose (GEL–CMC) hydrogels containing l-cysteine (l-Cys) as edible coating systems for maintaining the postharvest quality of button mushrooms (Agaricus bisporus) during refrigerated storage. Four l-Cys concentrations (2, 3, 4 and 5 g L−1) were incorporated into GEL–CMC hydrogels, with a GEL–CMC formulation without l-Cys serving as the control.

RESULTS

Incorporation of l-Cys modified the physicochemical, functional, mechanical, barrier and thermal properties of the hydrogels and hydrogel films in a concentration-dependent manner. Fourier transform infrared and X-ray diffraction analyses indicated changes in the molecular environment and structural organization of the GEL–CMC matrix following l-Cys incorporation, whereas scanning electroni microscopy observations revealed concentration-dependent changes in film morphology. The l-Cys-containing formulations also exhibited differences in DPPH (i.e. 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl) radical-scavenging activity and total flavonoid content. During refrigerated storage, mushrooms coated with l-Cys-containing formulations generally showed improved retention of quality attributes, including reduced weight loss and browning, better firmness retention, lower malondialdehyde accumulation and lower microbial counts, although the magnitude of the effects varied among quality parameters and l-Cys concentrations.

CONCLUSION

GEL–CMC/l-Cys hydrogel coatings showed promising potential for postharvest preservation of button mushrooms under refrigerated storage conditions. Incorporation of l-Cys provided an approach for modifying the performance of the GEL–CMC coating matrix and improving the retention of selected mushroom quality attributes during storage. These findings support the potential of GEL–CMC/l-Cys hydrogels as edible coating systems for postharvest applications and provide a basis for further optimization of their formulation and application conditions. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
